name: Underdog
label: Revelation
lede: Two skaters met at CBGB and built a hardcore band that could sing. They handed a guitar to the first Black skater on a Thrasher cover, made one album, and split the minute the van got home.

eras.title: Two skaters, one week out of their old bands
eras.text: Richie Birkenhead had just come out of the Numskuls and Russ Iglay had just walked away from Murphy's Law. They met at CBGB and started a band that wanted hardcore's speed with a real melody on top, and a skate ramp somewhere in the background.

years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Ice and I
years.h: A week after leaving Murphy's Law, Iglay starts Underdog
years.p: Birkenhead sings and Russ "Wheeler" Iglay plays bass, after meeting at CBGB. Danny Derella takes guitar and Greg Pierce the drums.
years.xp:
Iglay says Underdog came together about a week after he left [[Murphy's Law|4a9fae02-7de0-4cb8-97d7-1fd790d9675e]]. Birkenhead had been fronting the Numskuls since 1983.

Both were serious skaters. Birkenhead has named Tony Alva, Duane Peters and Neil Blender as heroes right alongside [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]], [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] and SSD.

years.h: The first demo already has a skate anthem on it
years.p: Eight songs cut at Electric Reels in December, among them True Blue, Say It (To My Face)! and Frontside Grind. Derella is on guitar, Pierce on drums.

years.h: Birkenhead spends a year on guitar in Youth of Today
years.p: He plays in Ray Cappo's [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] through 1986, then leaves to put everything into Underdog.

years.h: Pierce goes to college in Florida; Dean Joseph takes the drums
years.p: Pierce leaves after a few months and a handful of shows. Joseph, of Good Humor, plays in both bands until Underdog starts touring.
years.xp: Iglay also remembers a second guitarist, Arthur, who made the band sound bigger but left after an early tour. In Iglay's telling, Underdog toured loose, Arthur took it seriously, and the two didn't mix.

eras.title: Sunday matinees and Jersey Shore Elks halls
eras.text: Underdog became a fixture at the CBGB matinees and down the Jersey Shore. Birkenhead could scream one line and croon the next; their booking agent later said his voice went from guttural to choirboy mid-song.

years.h: Underdog's whole CBGB matinee is on tape
years.p: April 17, 1988: Birkenhead and Iglay at the front of the Bowery stage, a full set filmed and passed around for decades before Revelation put it online.

years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · YouTube: Underdog, Amalgamated
years.h: The Belmar Elks Club is the show Jersey kids keep mentioning
years.p: Iglay says the mid-1988 Belmar night was the one people brought up for years. City Gardens in Trenton and the Stone Pony in Asbury Park became regular stops too.
years.xp: The band did not stay on the Jersey Shore. A VHS master of the full set at the Amalgamated Transit Union Hall in St. Louis, July 29, 1988, shows Underdog on the road that summer.

years.h: Don Fury records seven songs and Caroline signs Underdog
years.p: The fall demo at Don Fury's Manhattan studio holds Over the Edge, Mass Movement and The Vanishing Point. Caroline Records hears the tape and signs the band.

eras.title: A pro skater on guitar, then home for good
eras.text: Underdog finally made an album, with a Thrasher cover star on guitar, and took it across the country. It was the peak, and it was the end.

years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Wikipedia: Chuck Treece
years.h: Tom Groholski brings Chuck Treece to the band
years.p: The pro skater introduces Underdog to [[Chuck Treece|ef661f53-d4b4-4903-811c-f3dcb1b970f3]], the Philadelphia skater and [[McRad|df55082c-8a17-448d-a9c9-e3c7f00546a7]] leader who in 1984 became the first African-American skater on a Thrasher cover. Treece completes the classic lineup.
years.xp: Treece was a sponsored pro from 1982 to 1990, riding for Santa Cruz, Powell-Peralta and Airwalk, and he'd go on to play with [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]. With Birkenhead, Iglay and Joseph, he's the lineup most fans mean when they say Underdog.

years.h: Pushead puts Underdog on Thrasher's Skate Rock Volume 7
years.p: Iglay says Pushead picked the band for Thrasher's cassette-only Skate Rock series, the skate world's own mixtape.

q: Underdog always existed on the fringes.
years.h: The Vanishing Point, with a little reggae in it
years.p: Eleven songs for Caroline, produced by Don Fury. Most are the Over the Edge demo songs, rebuilt with Treece on guitar.
years.xp:
Caroline pressed it on LP, CD and cassette in the US, with a Belgian CD for Europe. Tracks include Over the Edge, Back to Back, Blindside and the title track.

Birkenhead never loved the hardcore tag. Underdog, he told Noisecreep, always sat on the edges of it.

years.big: Once we came home from that tour, that was pretty much the end
years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Finding Connecticut
years.h: The Vanishing Point tour is the last thing Underdog do
years.p: Russ Iglay on the national tour for The Vanishing Point, the band's best run ever. Once the van got back to New York, Underdog was finished.
years.xp: There was no big blowup on the record. The tour went well, the band went on hiatus, and the hiatus turned permanent. Birkenhead was already writing songs that didn't fit hardcore at all.

eras.title: Into Another, and two demos on one record
eras.text: Birkenhead went somewhere much stranger with Into Another. Revelation, the label from his old Youth of Today circle, later put both Underdog demos on one LP.

years.src: Ice and I · Wikipedia: Richie Birkenhead
years.h: Birkenhead starts Into Another with Drew Thomas of Bold
years.p: [[Into Another|c235e5fd-4144-4e53-95ff-b33dc5f239c8]] sign to Revelation and later to Hollywood Records.
years.xp: Birkenhead's explanation for moving on from Underdog was stagnation, not boredom: he felt he couldn't express himself fully in the old band.

years.cap: Richie Birkenhead with Into Another, Los Angeles, 1995
years.h: Revelation puts both Underdog demos on one LP
years.p: REV 28 has the December 1985 True Blue demo on side A and the fall 1988 Over the Edge demo on side B. First press: 1,900 black and 300 blue.

eras.title: Benefits, Japan and the fight for CBGB
eras.text: A reissue pulled Underdog back in 1998, and after that they came out whenever something mattered: a benefit, a festival, the fight to save CBGB. Birkenhead, Iglay and Joseph kept showing up.

years.h: Go-Kart reissues The Vanishing Point on red vinyl
years.p: LP, red vinyl and CD, with live bonus tracks on the CD.

years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · YouTube: Underdog live at Coney
years.h: Underdog reunite at Asbury Park's Convention Hall
years.p: The Alive and Well benefit comes first, then a tour for Go-Kart with Jay from American Standard on drums and Matt Dolan on guitar.
years.xp: The band's reunion-era set at Coney Island High on September 23, 1998 is on video, a full show from the Go-Kart tour year.

years.cap: Underdog in Essen, Germany, March 31, 2006, their first European show
years.h: Underdog play benefits to save CBGB
years.p: The original core plays benefit shows for CBGB, first with [[Killing Time|9e3c100d-51c9-43da-b21d-4dcead9a3142]]. Iglay says later dates put them on bills with [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]] and the Stimulators.

years.cap: Richie Birkenhead sings into the crowd, Rivolta, Marghera, Italy, April 4, 2006
years.h: Europe first, then Japan's Magma Festival
years.p: Underdog's first European show was March 31, 2006 in Essen, with Marghera, Italy four days later. Japan's Magma Festival came in 2007, 18 years after The Vanishing Point.

years.h: Burning Fight Festival, Chicago
years.p: Underdog join the reunion-heavy Burning Fight Festival.

eras.title: Matchless, sober, and nine kids later
eras.text: Underdog never made new music and never pretended they would. They collected the old songs on Bridge Nine and kept playing them, with a Floorpunch guitarist filling out the classic lineup.

years.cap: Richie Birkenhead with Underdog at United Blood Fest, April 3, 2011
years.src: Double Cross: Russ Iglay · Revelation Records
years.h: Bridge Nine puts every Underdog song on Matchless
years.p: B9R133 gathers The Vanishing Point and the demos, 26 tracks, as a gatefold double LP and CD.
years.xp:
Iglay says talks with Revelation were moving slowly, so he emailed Bridge Nine's Chris Wrenn, who answered within hours. Iglay liked the label's hard deadlines.

He also credited his own sobriety for how well Underdog was going. New songs? The band's nine kids made that close to impossible, he said, and Underdog wouldn't want it any other way.

years.h: Underdog play an all-ages show at Space Ballroom in Hamden
years.p: Birkenhead, Iglay and Joseph, with Marc "Zev" Zeveney of [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]] on guitar.
